html:
The Tłı̨chǫ, once called Dogrib, are a Dene people of the Northwest Territories, Canada, living between Great Slave Lake and Great Bear Lake; Tłı̨chǫ Ndè means Tłı̨chǫ land. They speak an Athabaskan language and traditionally hunted barren-ground caribou at the edge of the tundra and fished the many lakes.

In the early 1800s rivalry over the fur trade led to bloody fighting with the Yellowknives under Akaitcho, until the Tłı̨chǫ leader Edzo made a famous peace with him in the 1820s. They traded furs with the Hudson's Bay Company and signed Treaty 11 in 1921. In 2005 the Tłı̨chǫ Agreement gave them self-government and ownership of a large block of land around Behchokǫ̀ and other communities, one of the first such agreements in the north. Their neighbours are the Sahtú Dene to the north and the Yellowknives to the east.
